Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking TideBank's RFP. We’re putting together the section on dedicated reservations and have a few specific questions that need clarifying for our procurement and infra teams before we can finalize the mutual action plan. High level: we need to validate how Redwood maps customer workloads to GPU families, how burst capacity is billed/allocated, and what guardrails exist to prevent noisy-neighbor impact.

Can you provide: 
- Typical GPU families you recommend for mixed chat+embedding workloads (e.g., A100 vs H100 vs L4), including per-GPU throughput baselines for 2k and 8k token workloads.
- How reserved capacity and burst lanes interact — is burst carved out of the commitment or billed separately? What controls prevent burst from starving reservation SLOs?
- Fallback behavior (model variant swap, region failover) when reserved capacity is saturated.
- Any suggested reservation profiles for an initial 100k monthly requests with a 20% burst headroom for first 90 days.

I appreciate any attachments/workbooks you can share (CSV or spreadsheet preferred). We’re aiming to run procurement review next Tuesday (6/29).

Best,
Maya Patel
Sr. Cloud Architect, TideBank

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear set of asks. We put together an initial workbook and short appendix that addresses each point and includes conservative throughput baselines we use internally. Key highlights pasted below; workbook attached.

Summary highlights:
- Recommended GPU families: H100 for high-throughput/low-latency chat at 8k+ context, A100 for mixed workload predictability, L4 for cost-sensitive embedding-heavy tails. We include quantified qps/token baselines in the workbook.
- Burst model: burst is implemented as a separate pool (burst lane) that is billed at on-demand RPU rates and is not deducted from the committed capacity; customers can optionally configure a burst budget that auto-throttles when reservation SLOs would be impacted.
- Guardrails: we implement an admission controller that prioritizes pinned reservation traffic; burst requests are preemptible and tagged with a lower priority. Preemption is only used when latency SLOs for pinned routes are at risk.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback policy can swap to compatible quantized model variants (same family) and optionally route to a secondary region if enabled in the M.A.P.

Attached: fleet-fitment-workbook.csv (GPU mapping + throughput baselines), redwood-mapping-appendix.pdf (technical notes). Also attached a draft mutual action plan.

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute sizing workshop next week to walk the workbook and confirm your expected mixture of embedding vs chat. Lauren will help with contract-level questions and I’ll own the technical fit. Can you do 6/28 at 10am PT or 6/29 at 9am PT?

Thanks,

Hi Maya — quick answers to the items you flagged; attaching an updated workbook tab ("Burst & Billing") and a short smoke-test checklist.

1) Mixed reservations: we don't force dual committed invoices for multi-family usage. Typical pattern we recommend: commit to a baseline family (A100) sized for steady-state; enable an H100 burst lane that operates as an on-demand pool. The burst pool is separate from the commit for accounting, but we can include a billing cap (safety budget) on the burst lane that, when exceeded, will auto-close burst consumption and revert to reservation-only. That cap becomes part of the M.A.P.

2) Burst billing options:
- Option A: pure on-demand (no cap) — simplest, transparent RPU pricing.
- Option B: on-demand with a negotiated monthly burst cap (we invoice reserved + burst capped overage). If you want predictable runway we typically negotiate a capped overage with a step discount at volume thresholds.

3) Preemption observability: yes. We emit structured events to customer audit logs and can stream them to your SIEM or a pullable logs endpoint. Events include request id, route, policy triggered, and preemption reason.

4) Perf test harness: we maintain a lightweight stress harness (open-source reference) and a Redwood-run smoke test that validates tail latency and model output parity against a pinned prompt set. We’ll share the harness and can coordinate an authenticated smoke run from CloudOps.

We updated the workbook with sample reservation profiles for 100k monthly requests with a 20% burst headroom; tab = "SuggestedProfiles_100k". See the Drive link below. If that looks good we’ll convert to numbers for the M.A.P. and schedule the smoke run.
